data.title: Chartwell: Buy Rating Reiterated as Growth Outlook Remains Robust; $27 Price Target Unchanged Amid Valuation Discount
data.description:
In a report released on September 11, Jonathan Kelcher from TD Cowen maintained a Buy rating on Chartwell Retirement Residences, with a price target of C$27.00.

Jonathan Kelcher has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, including Chartwell’s strong growth profile and attractive valuation after the recent share price pullback. He expects the company to deliver among the fastest AFFO and NAV growth in its peer group, supported by robust retirement housing fundamentals and limited new supply, which should allow occupancy to surpass management’s targets and drive rent and margin expansion.

Kelcher also highlights that a large portion of Chartwell’s portfolio still has meaningful occupancy upside, reinforcing the potential for continued double‑digit NAV growth. Despite this outlook, the stock trades at a steep discount of about 46% versus U.S. peers, far wider than historical norms, and he views this as unjustified given similar growth prospects and positive estimate revisions, supporting his unchanged $27 price target and Buy recommendation.

data.title: Analyst Reiterates Buy on Perdoceo, Sees Upside with Unchanged $44 Price Target After South University Acquisition
data.description:
Alexander Paris, an analyst from Barrington, reiterated the Buy rating on Perdoceo Education. The associated price target remains the same with $44.00.

Alexander Paris has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, including the accretive acquisition of South University and reaffirmed guidance. He views the South University deal as strategically attractive given its strong health sciences programs, immediate contribution to adjusted operating income beginning in 2027, and reasonable purchase multiples versus the target’s trailing revenue and profit metrics.

Paris also emphasizes Perdoceo’s solid financial position and valuation appeal, noting substantial cash on hand, no long-term debt, and a dividend that has recently been increased. He believes the stock’s trading multiples remain materially below those of comparable postsecondary education companies, and with the $44 price target unchanged, he sees meaningful upside potential from current levels, supported by expected growth in revenue, earnings and profitability.
